question_title: Will the U.S. and Argentina have signed a new 123 civil nuclear cooperation agreement as of September 10, 2026?
summary:
Status quo is NO and the window is only 22 days. Verified independently: no signing has occurred, and the most recent reporting (Aug 10, 2026, unnamed Casa Rosada sources, replicated across several Argentine outlets) says the technical text is finalized but the Cancillería is still "coordinating with Washington the diplomatic aspects to arrange the signing during the coming months," targeting "before the end of the year." No date, venue, or ceremony has been announced by State, DOE, or the Cancillería.

The calendar is the dominant consideration. Milei's confirmed 2026 US itinerary (reported Aug 9) is UNGA in late September, Washington on October 14, and the G20 in Miami in December — FM Quirno accompanies on the latter two. The IAEA General Conference is also late September. Every natural signing occasion falls after the September 10 resolution date, and there is nothing on the books before it. Deadline pressure is minimal: the 1997 agreement runs to October 16, 2027, and even with the post-signature presidential determination plus 90 days of continuous congressional session, signing as late as mid-2027 still permits entry into force before expiry.

I modeled the signing date as a hazard process over Aug 19 – Dec 31, mixing three hazard shapes (uniform 35%, event-clustered 45%, back-loaded toward year-end 20%) with P(signed by year-end) ~ Beta(5.8, 4.2), mean 0.58. Result: 5.2%, stable in a 3–7% band across reasonable variants; the grid corners run 1.9% to 14.0%.

The genuine case for a higher number is that the US–Saudi 123 (signed July 22, 2026 at DOE) and the US–Paraguay civil-nuclear MOU (August 4, 2026 at State) were both minister-level ceremonies with no summit attached, announced only days ahead — so "nothing announced today" is weaker evidence than it looks, and the text being finished means the residual barrier is purely scheduling. That is why I do not go below 3%. But the criteria are strict: an extension, an MOU on the Paraguay template, initialing, or a "negotiations concluded" statement all resolve NO, and those are the more likely near-term outputs of a warming relationship. I settle at 5%, slightly above the factor sum (3.6% off my 9.5% anchor) to leave room for the short-notice-ceremony channel.

factors.description: No bilateral event on the calendar in the Aug 19 – Sep 10 window. Milei's confirmed 2026 US itinerary (reported Aug 9, 2026) is UNGA New York in late September (~Sep 22-26), Washington on October 14 for a Hispanic Heritage Month conference, and the G20 in Miami in December — FM Quirno accompanies on the latter two. The IAEA General Conference is also late September. Every natural signing venue falls AFTER the resolution date.

Argentine government's own framing (Aug 10, 2026, unnamed Casa Rosada sources) is 'coordinating with Washington the diplomatic aspects to arrange the signing during the coming months' with a target of 'before the end of the year' — plural months, not weeks. No date, venue, or ceremony has been announced by State, DOE, or the Cancillería.

Very low deadline pressure. The 1997 agreement runs to Oct 16, 2027. Even allowing for the post-signature presidential determination plus 90 days of continuous congressional session, signing anytime through roughly mid-2027 still permits entry into force before expiry. Nothing forces action in the next three weeks.

Resolution criteria are narrow and exclude several plausible near-term news events. Fine print bars a mere extension of the 1997 agreement. An MOU/NCMOU (the Paraguay template), initialing of text, or a joint statement announcing 'negotiations concluded' would all still resolve NO. Only an actual signature by authorized representatives counts.

Substantive negotiating work is done: Casa Rosada sources say the technical drafting was finalized (text fully articulated at the Feb 25-27, 2026 JSCNEC meeting in Washington) and only diplomatic scheduling remains. This removes the usual multi-month tail of textual haggling and means a ceremony could be arranged on short notice.

Trump-administration civil-nuclear momentum, including in Latin America: US–Saudi 123 agreement signed July 22, 2026 (Sec. Wright + Prince Abdulaziz at DOE); US–Paraguay civil-nuclear MOU signed Aug 4, 2026 (Rubio + FM Ramírez Lezcano at the State Dept). Both were minister-level ceremonies requiring no summit, and such ceremonies are typically announced only days in advance — so absence of an announcement today is weaker evidence than it would be for a leaders-level event.

**Forecast: 5%** — the U.S. and Argentina are unlikely to have signed a new 123 agreement by September 10, 2026.

## Key findings

**Status quo is NO, and the window is only 22 days.** I verified independently that no signing has occurred — the most recent relevant reporting is August 10, 2026.

**The Argentine government's own timeline points past the deadline.** Wire copy sourced to unnamed Casa Rosada officials (replicated across ANRoca, NoticiasNet, El Cordillerano, Diario Panorama, cholilaonline) says the technical text was finalized at the February 2026 JSCNEC meeting, but the Cancillería is still "coordinating with Washington the diplomatic aspects to arrange the signing **during the coming months**," targeting "before the end of the year." No date, venue, or ceremony announced.

**Every natural signing occasion falls after September 10.** Milei's confirmed 2026 U.S. itinerary (reported Aug 9): UNGA in late September, Washington on October 14, G20 Miami in December — FM Quirno accompanies on the latter two. The IAEA General Conference is also late September. Nothing is on the books before the resolution date.

**Deadline pressure is minimal.** The 1997 agreement runs to October 16, 2027. Even with the presidential determination plus 90 days of continuous congressional session, signing as late as mid-2027 still allows entry into force before expiry.

## Method

I modeled the signing date as a hazard process over Aug 19 – Dec 31, mixing three hazard shapes (uniform 35%, event-clustered 45%, back-loaded 20%) with P(signed by year-end) ~ Beta(5.8, 4.2), mean 0.58. Result: **5.2%**, stable in a 3–7% band; grid corners run 1.9% to 14.0%.

## The strongest counterargument

The U.S.–Saudi 123 (July 22, 2026, at DOE) and U.S.–Paraguay civil-nuclear MOU (August 4, 2026, at State) were both minister-level ceremonies with no summit attached, announced only days ahead. That weakens the calendar argument and is why I don't go below 3%. Cutting the other way: the criteria are strict — an extension, an MOU on the Paraguay template, or a "negotiations concluded" statement all resolve NO, and those are the likelier near-term outputs.

One tooling note worth flagging: the `research()` call returned 79,733 characters that overflowed to a path outside the Read/Grep allowlist, so none of it was accessible. I reconstructed the analysis entirely from direct searches.

resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if, as of September 10, 2026 (0:00 UTC), the government of the United States and the government of Argentina have formally signed a new bilateral Agreement for Cooperation Concerning Peaceful Uses of Nuclear Energy (a "123 Agreement" under Section 123 of the U.S. Atomic Energy Act). Resolution is based on an official announcement by the U.S. Department of State or U.S. Department of Energy, an official statement from the government of Argentina (e.g. the Cancillería or the office responsible for nuclear affairs), or reporting from [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) confirming that authorized representatives of both governments have signed the text of the new agreement. If no such signing has occurred as of that time, the question resolves NO.
fine_print: A mere extension of the existing 1997 agreement (rather than a newly signed replacement agreement) does not count.

input.anchor: Uniform-hazard reading of the Argentine government's own stated target: P(signed by Dec 31, 2026) ≈ 0.58 × (22 days / 134 days remaining in 2026) ≈ 9.5%. Source: Aug 10, 2026 Argentine wire reporting citing Casa Rosada officials ("antes de fin de año").
input.assessment:
QUESTION TYPE: Predictive, short-horizon (22 days), with status quo = NO.

STATUS QUO: No signing has occurred. Verified independently of the question description — the most recent relevant reporting is Aug 10, 2026, and neither State/DOE nor the Cancillería has announced a signature.

PRE-PUBLICATION TRAP CHECK: The February 2026 JSCNEC meeting advanced/finalized a draft text, and Spanish coverage sometimes uses 'rubricar' loosely. But (a) that predates publication (Aug 19, 2026) with no explicit start date in the criteria, so Case 2 applies and it cannot resolve YES; and (b) the question description explicitly acknowledges the Feb meeting while stating no signing has occurred. No trap here.

QUANTITATIVE MODEL: I modeled the signing date as a hazard process over the 134 days from Aug 19 to Dec 31, 2026, mixing three hazard shapes — uniform (35%), event-clustered around UNGA/Oct 14 Washington/Dec G20 (45%), and back-loaded toward a year-end deadline rush (20%) — with P(signed by year-end) drawn from Beta(5.8, 4.2), mean 0.58. Result: P(YES) = 5.2%. Sensitivity across the corners of the grid runs 1.9% (back-loaded, p_year=0.45) to 14.0% (uniform, p_year=0.85). The estimate is stable in the 3–7% band for any plausible combination that does not assume a purely uniform hazard AND a near-certain year-end signing.

CASE FOR NO (dominant): Nothing is scheduled. The government's own stated horizon is 'coming months.' Every high-visibility venue is after Sep 10. There is no deadline forcing function for another year. And the criteria exclude the softer outcomes (MOU, extension, initialing) that a warming relationship is more likely to produce in the very near term.

CASE FOR YES: The text is done, so the residual barrier is purely scheduling — and the Trump administration has demonstrated in the last month that it will hold minister-level civil-nuclear signing ceremonies at State/DOE on short notice with no summit attached (Saudi Jul 22, Paraguay Aug 4). Argentina is the most-aligned government in the region and an obvious next candidate. A Quirno or Ramos Nápoli trip to Washington could materialize with a week's notice.

SYNTHESIS: My factor sum implies ~3.6%; my Monte Carlo gives 5.2%. I settle at 5%, slightly above the factor sum, because the short-notice-ceremony channel is real and my factor list arguably over-penalizes the calendar (the Paraguay and Saudi signings prove a summit is not required). But it stays well below 10% because the specific 22-day window contains no known trigger and the government itself is signalling a later timeline.
input.calibration_notes: Anchor 9.5% → final 5%. The divergence is downward and driven by one dominant, well-evidenced consideration: the calendar. The anchor assumes uniform hazard; the actual calendar puts every plausible venue after Sep 10, which mechanically shifts mass out of the window. Status quo persistence applies with full force here — this is exactly the class of question (announced diplomatic intention, no scheduled date) where forecasters overestimate the dramatic near-term outcome. Not hedging toward 50%: the evidence supports a confidently low number. I resisted going below 3% because minister-level 123/nuclear signings in this administration have been announced with only days of lead time, so 'nothing announced today' does not rule out a signing three weeks out.
input.key_uncertainties: (1) Whether an unannounced Quirno or Ramos Nápoli trip to Washington is already being scheduled for late August/early September — anonymous-source reporting would not necessarily have surfaced this. (2) Whether P(signed by year-end 2026) is really ~0.58; if the Casa Rosada sources are well-informed and the US side is equally ready, it could be 0.75+, which raises P(YES) to ~6-7% under my hazard mix. (3) Whether the US side has any remaining substantive reservations — the Argentine reporting is one-sided (Casa Rosada only), and I found no US-side confirmation that the text is final. If Washington is not actually ready, both p_year and P(YES) fall.
input.tool_audit: mcp__search__web_search: highly productive — five queries surfaced the decisive Aug 10, 2026 Argentine wire story (replicated across ANRoca, NoticiasNet, El Cordillerano, Diario Panorama, LCR, cholilaonline), Milei's confirmed US travel calendar (Aug 9, 2026), and the US–Saudi (Jul 22) and US–Paraguay (Aug 4) 2026 nuclear signings. mcp__search__fetch_url: worked well on two Argentine outlets, confirming 'technical drafting finalized / diplomatic coordination underway / no date or venue.' mcp__sandbox__execute_code: used for the hazard-mixture Monte Carlo; worked first try. mcp__research__research: FAILED usefully-but-awkwardly — it returned 79,733 characters that exceeded the token limit and were spilled to a file under /home/pfftz/.claude/.lup-sessions/..., which is OUTSIDE the permitted Read/Grep roots, so both Read and Grep were denied and I could not access any of it. That research was effectively wasted; I reconstructed everything with direct search instead.
input.update_triggers: Would move me sharply UP (to 40%+): a State Department or Cancillería media note announcing a signing ceremony date; a announced visit by FM Quirno or Sec. Ramos Nápoli to Washington (or Rubio/Wright to Buenos Aires) before Sep 10; a DOE/NNSA press advisory naming Argentina. Would move me UP moderately (to ~12-15%): US-side confirmation that the text is final and awaiting signature, or reporting that the signing is targeted for 'the coming weeks' rather than months. Would move me DOWN (to ~2%): reporting that the signing is slated for the Oct 14 Washington visit or the December G20, or that an unresolved issue (e.g. enrichment/reprocessing consent rights, uranium supply terms) has reopened.
input.process_reflection: The one real friction point was severe: mcp__research__research overflowed the token cap and spilled its entire output to a path that the Read and Grep permission allowlist does not include. The tool result even instructed me to read the file in chunks, but every access route was denied. That is a hard scaffolding bug — the overflow directory should be added to the allowlist, or the research tool should truncate/summarize rather than spill. As it stands an expensive Opus sub-agent call produced zero usable output. Recommend either (a) allowlisting the .lup-sessions tool-results directory, or (b) having research() return a bounded summary with the full text as an optional follow-up.\n\nOtherwise the scaffolding fit this question well. It is a short-horizon status-quo question where the decisive evidence is calendar-shaped, and the guidance to model the underlying quantity (here, signing date) rather than argue YES/NO narratively was the right frame — turning it into a hazard-over-time problem made the sensitivity analysis natural and kept me from anchoring on the warm-relations narrative. I did not use subforecast(); decomposition would have added nothing over a single hazard model. One capability gap: there is no tool for querying official government press-release feeds (state.gov media notes, cancilleria.gob.ar, energy.gov newsroom) directly, so I had to infer 'nothing announced' from the absence of search hits, which is weaker evidence than a clean feed check would be.
